execution_environments.worker: patchgate-key-challenge-worker.js, deployed only after approved main enrollment; Web Crypto only, no Node imports
execution_environments.provisioner: scripts/provision-patchgate-challenge-keys.mjs, Node22 on Actions; imports fs and node:crypto explicitly; it uploads the separate worker module, never itself

dispositions.evidence: verifyChallenge/createPublicKey/verify/key.export and fs execute in Node22 on Actions with explicit node:crypto/fs imports. The uploaded Worker only uses crypto.subtle. Both native review outputs mixed these distinct executables; worker and provisioner are exercised together by CI.

The caller of canonicalChallenge constructs every signed payload from fixed fields and a 64-hex nonce. /challenge rejects any additional field, subject, role, non-JSON input or invalid nonce. The public arbitrary-payload helper capability suggested in the finding does not exist.

Exact secret comparison is intentional. Stripping arbitrary BOM/whitespace would accept altered credentials. Invalid authentication returns401; malformed provisioning/secret errors produce a bounded sanitized blocker. No silent success is recorded.

Public identity is not sufficient for enrollment: the provisioner imports DER-SPKI and verifies a fresh actual signature, exact public key and all bindings. Malformed public configuration returns a blocked report and cannot enable A2.

Ed25519 key generation requires private key memory. Private PKCS8 is sent over HTTPS only to fixed CF Secrets API; fixture assertion verifies no secret in report. Secrets deliberately survive redeployment to test persistence; rotating them would defeat the test. JavaScript provides no guaranteed memory zeroization; this residual is disclosed, not certified against a claimed NIST standard.

Separate targets intentionally generate independent pairs. Worker fixes id/provider correspondence and verifier checks provider, executor, public key and signed payload. The opposite-provider and other-public-key fixture tests fail.

No arbitrary source input is accepted. Upload uses the fixed repository worker source and fixed public key, preserves secrets, then repeats a nonce proof with the same public key. Source hash is a configured upload binding, not independent remote code attestation. A malicious later source change would be a new reviewed deployment, not authorized here.

Caller generates a cryptographic fresh nonce and requires that exact nonce in the signed payload. verifyChallenge checks signed at_utc against current time within120s and rejects altered nonce/provider/key/source. A caller timestamp header adds no proof.

Existing LTZZZ_AGENT_TOKEN authenticates only nonce-challenge route here, which cannot attest A2 roles, call a model or move funds. Sharing that service credential is a management boundary, not equivalent to private-key leakage. Before production role signing, use scoped independently managed auth and audit actual model-to-role binding. No TLS interception evidence was observed; HTTPS redirects are denied.

limitations: This disposition is by the author/controller, not a replacement for Claude independent review.
All original FAIL text and native receipts are preserved; no repeated model call was made to obtain approve.
No actual CF API enrollment or signing-key restart proof has occurred, and no key/role enters trust automatically.
No A2 /attest endpoint, wallet signing, payment, arbitrary payload signing or native model generation is provided by these candidate services.
Current tested route proves only key correspondence/persistence with a fake transport until live main enrollment is separately run.
